title: An invariant fibrewise dense affine open from generic effectivity over a trait
statement: Let $B\to C$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}C$ (localizations at all nonzero elements). Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X'\to S'$ be smooth, separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Give $X'$ a descent datum $\alpha$ relative to $S'/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Suppose its generic restriction is effective, with specified $K$-scheme $X_0$ and isomorphism $X_0\times_KL\simeq X'_L$ realizing that restriction [def-pc-base-change]. There exist an affine $S$-scheme $U$, an invariant affine open $U'\subseteq X'$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and an isomorphism $U\times_SS'\simeq U'$ realizing the restricted datum. Here invariant means $\alpha(p_0^*U')=p_1^*U'$ over $S'\times_SS'$. The open $U'$ is dense in every geometric fibre of $X'\to S'$. Moreover, $U_K$ has an open immersion into $X_0$ whose base change is the inclusion $U'_L\subseteq X'_L$. Empty schemes and empty special fibres are allowed. No group law is assumed.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, final paragraphs, printed pp.161-162 (PDF pp.167-168), using Lemma 6 and the quasi-finite locus of affinization, followed by the first paragraph of case (a), p.160, and BLR 6.4 Lemma 4 to shrink the effective open to an affine. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: The affine map $p:S'\to S$ is flat and surjective by the affine flatness criterion and faithful-flat spectrum surjectivity; it is quasi-compact by affine-morphism permanence, hence is a singleton fpqc covering. The DVR definition makes $B,C$ principal ideal domains, hence Noetherian normal domains of dimension one. Smooth-trait infrastructure makes $X'$ Noetherian and regular with finitely many pairwise disjoint special-fibre components and schematically dense generic fibre. Its open subschemes remain Noetherian; their inclusions are quasi-compact and of finite type, and they remain smooth by smooth open restriction. Separatedness of any such open over $S'$ follows directly by restricting the closed diagonal of $X'/S'$. These observations justify all later applications to open subschemes. A uniformizer of $B$ maps to a unit times a positive power of a uniformizer of $C$: surjectivity on spectra forces the closed point to map to the closed point. Thus $C\otimes_B K=L$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof setup, pp.161-162; standard affine fpqc and smooth-trait properties recorded in the cited nodes.

proof.text: The scheme $X_0$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $K$: its pullback along the fpqc field extension $L/K$ is $X'_L$, which has those properties by base change. Apply fpqc descent of smoothness, separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compactness. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole ring); hence $X_0$ is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components. The dense affine-cover existence statement supplies an affine open $V_0\subseteq X_0$ containing every component generic point, so $V_0$ is dense. Density persists under extension to $L$ by smooth fibrewise-density base change. If $X_0$ is empty then schematic density of the generic fibre forces $X'$ empty; take $U=U'=\varnothing$. Henceforth allow nonempty $X_0$ and choose $V_0$ as above.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, first paragraph: choose an affine dense open of the descended generic scheme.

proof.text: Take the reduced induced closed complement $Z_0=(X_0\setminus V_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, set $Z_L=(Z_0)_L$ in $X'_L$, and let $Z'$ be its schematic closure in $X'$. We retain this base-changed closed subscheme structure, rather than reducing after scalar extension; it is therefore preserved by the specified generic datum even for inseparable $L/K$. The horizontal-closure lemma shows that $Y'=X'\setminus |Z'|$ is dense in every geometric fibre and has affine generic fibre $(V_0)_L$. It is invariant: the generic datum preserves $Z_L$ as a closed subscheme, and schematic image commutes with flat pullback to either projection $S'\times_S S'\to S'$. These projections are flat by fpqc base change. The immersion defining the closure is quasi-compact, since $X'_L\to X'$ is the principal open defined by a base uniformizer and $Z_L$ is closed in it. Hence the cited flat schematic-image theorem applies even if the double overlap is non-Noetherian. Complements of the identified pulled-back closed subschemes agree, giving the restricted datum on $Y'$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, affine-generic reduction; flat schematic-image compatibility is Stacks Tag 081I.

proof.text: For any invariant open $Y\subseteq Y'$ whose generic fibre is $(V_0)_L$, form $A_Y=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ and its canonical affinization $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A_Y$. Flat base change of global sections identifies both pulled-back affine targets over the double overlap with the spectra of the corresponding section rings. The isomorphism of the two pulled-back copies of $Y$ therefore induces an isomorphism of these targets, intertwining the two maps $a_Y$: their section maps both send a pure tensor $b\otimes r$ to the product of the pulled-back sections $b,r$. Functoriality gives the cocycle. The affinization-locus lemma gives a quasi-compact quasi-affine open $W(Y)$ containing the whole generic fibre, and meeting the special fibre whenever $Y$ does. By the cited base-change compatibility of the quasi-finite locus, its pullbacks agree under the datum. Thus $W(Y)$ is invariant and its datum is effective by quasi-affine fpqc effectivity. No finite generation of $A_Y$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, assertions (i)-(iii) for the quasi-finite locus, and 6.1 Theorem 4; Stacks Tag 0247.

proof.text: For a smooth finite-type field scheme $F$ and an open $O$, its irreducible components are finitely many and pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subsets, by geometric normality and normal Noetherian component decomposition. Hence the union $H_F(O)$ of those meeting $O$ is open and closed. On each such component $D$, the nonempty open $O\cap D$ is dense; smooth fibrewise-density base change makes its pullback dense in $D_{k'}$ for every field extension $k'/k$, so it meets every component upstairs. Components disjoint from $O$ remain disjoint after pullback. Thus $H_F(O)$ commutes with field extension. For invariant $W(Y)\subseteq Y$, test this equality over residue fields of points of $S'\times_S S'$: the datum identifies the two copies of $W(Y)$, so identifies their component saturations on the closed fibres. Equality on all these point sets is equality of open-and-closed fibre subsets. Their complements in the two copies of $Y$ are consequently invariant open subschemes. This is a direct three-part argument from the cited statements, requiring no new component-saturation node.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, last paragraph; component decomposition: Stacks Tags 056T and 033M.

proof.text: Set $Y_0=Y'$ and, as long as $(Y_i)_k$ is nonempty, put $W_i=W(Y_i)$, let $H_i$ be the union of the special-fibre components of $Y_i$ meeting $W_i$, and set $Y_{i+1}=Y_i\setminus H_i$. Here $H_i$ is closed in the special fibre and therefore in $Y_i$; its complement is open and invariant by step 5. No generic point is removed, so $(Y_{i+1})_L=(V_0)_L$ remains affine and step 4 applies again. The special-fibre components are disjoint. Since $(W_i)_k$ is nonempty, at least one previously remaining component is removed, and none of the others changes. Induction on the finite number of special-fibre components therefore terminates. Include also the last $W(Y_N)=Y_N$ when its special fibre is empty; its whole scheme is its affine generic fibre. Let $V'=\bigcup_{i=0}^N W_i$. It is invariant, contains $(V_0)_L$, and meets every component of $Y'_k$ in a nonempty open. It is dense in that fibre, and step 5's field-extension argument makes this density geometric. Since $Y'$ was fibrewise geometrically dense in $X'$, so is $V'$. All opens here are finite type and smooth by step 1. When $Y'_k$ is empty this construction consists just of $W(Y')=Y'$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, final paragraph: finite iteration over special-fibre components.

proof.text: Each $W_i$ has effective restricted datum by step 4. Apply effective descent gluing on the invariant open cover $(W_i)$ of $V'$ to obtain a scheme $V$ over $S$ and a compatible isomorphism $V\times_S S'\simeq V'$. The scheme $V$ is smooth, separated and of finite type by the same four fpqc descent statements used in step 2. Its generic fibre has an open immersion into $X_0$: descend the compatible inclusion $V'_L=(V_0)_L\hookrightarrow X'_L$ along $L/K$ by fpqc morphism descent, then apply fpqc descent of open immersions. This uses morphism descent only after both schemes exist. The resulting morphism identifies $V_K$ with $V_0$ and realizes the specified generic identification.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, p.162, union of effective invariant opens, and case (a), p.160; Stacks Tags 0AP4 and 02W0.

proof.text: Apply the Dedekind smooth fibre-dense affine lemma to $V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, using that $B$ is Noetherian, integrally closed and of dimension one from step 1. It gives an affine open $U\subseteq V$ dense in every geometric fibre. Its pullback $U'=U\times_S S'$ is an invariant open of $V'$, hence of $X'$, with the prescribed effective isomorphism. It is affine because base change preserves affine morphisms and the base $S'$ is affine. Smooth fibrewise-density base change makes $U'$ fibrewise dense in $V'$. Composing dense open inclusions with $V'\subseteq X'$ gives density in every geometric fibre of $X'$. Finally the inclusion $U_K\subseteq V_K$ followed by the open immersion $V_K\hookrightarrow X_0$ is the requested open immersion; its base change is the original inclusion in $X'_L$ by its construction in step 7. The argument permits empty special fibres and the empty scheme.

source.place: BLR 6.5 proof, case (a), p.160, first paragraph, applying the affine-neighbourhood argument of BLR 6.4 Lemma 4.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q82-467473b07 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and all 8 steps; BLR is not in the local literature (WANTED), so I proved both new statements myself instead of trusting the source attribution. Horizontal-closure node: true by a dimension argument (Y normal, so its components are disjoint and flat over the DVR; the closure of a subset of generic dimension < d has special fibre of dimension ≤ d−1, which also holds on geometric fibres). Affinization-locus node: the open immersion follows from ZMT (Stacks 05K0, no finite presentation needed) plus normality, which makes the map birational. W_k ≠ ∅ follows from an affine open meeting every special component (given by the existing lem-sfb-dedekind-smooth-fibre-dense-affine) and an element g of the generic ring vanishing off that open, scaled so that min_j v_j(g) = 0. The node correctly does not claim W meets every component (example: P^1_R blown up at a special point, minus ∞, contracts E), which is why step 6 iterates. Neither new node duplicates an existing node (checked smooth-trait-principal-translate-cover, the closure-fibre-avoidance and closed-fibre-codimension nodes, scheme-image-flat-base-change, the affinization nodes) or restates a clause of the item. Steps: step 1 shows C⊗_B K = L because the closed point maps to the closed point; step 3 reduces downstairs before base change, which handles inseparable L/K, and invariance comes from flat base change of the schematic image (the morphism is quasi-compact; no Noetherian hypothesis on C⊗_B C is needed); step 4 gives invariance of W(Y) from flat base change of Γ for qcqs Y and base change of the quasi-finite locus, then quasi-affine fpqc effectivity; step 5 component saturation commutes with field extension (geometric normality); the step 6 induction is set up explicitly and terminates; steps 7–8 are gluing, descent and the Dedekind dense-affine node. The edge cases (empty scheme, empty special fibre) are handled.
